history.recommendation_text: The Board also recommended that the Administration continue to strengthen the guidance and monitoring of entities in reporting exceptions in order to improve entities’ compliance with the reporting requirements.
history.administration_response: The Administration considers this recommendation implemented and requests its closure. The Monitoring of Delegation of Authority Section in Business Transformation and Accountability Division provides a detailed analysis of the reporting compliance in its deep-dive review. The Business Transformation and Accountability Division has reiterated as the key message to entities that they are expected to continue to strengthen their reporting efforts and ensure that the exceptions granted are compliant with General Assembly resolutions and the applicable policy framework and that they are reported comprehensively and on time. The Division has also enhanced the exception log to capture and track cases where exceptions are approved by entities outside the scope of delegated authority, to increase the comprehensiveness of the monitoring on exceptions in the area of human resources. In addition to the annual deep-dive review, in 2021 the Division started to introduce ongoing review and monitoring throughout the year so as to bring exceptions or inconsistencies identified to the attention of the entities for rectification or reporting in the log. This approach was introduced to enable entities to take corrective action in a timely manner, to the extent possible, and to strengthen overall performance.The measures taken by the Administration, in particular regarding outreach to entities and issuance of more precise and hands- on guidance, have already led to improvements. For example, regarding consultants and individual contractors (covered in the Division’s guide on granting exceptions), the compliance rate for reporting rose from 30 per cent for consultants in 2020 to 71 per cent in 2021, and from 15 per cent for individual contractors to 31 per cent. (Details will be included in the human resources exceptions report of 2021, which will be available soon). Lastly, in order to further assist entities in monitoring their reporting performance, the Section will include an additional indicator to track compliance on reporting of the cases identified by the Division during the quarterly reviews.
history.board_assessment: Given the fact that the reporting compliance rate in 2021 was still relatively low, at 69 per cent after outreach by the Business Transformation and Accountability Division, the Board considers this recommendation to be under implementation.

It will consider the recommendation implemented with the roll-out, scheduled for April 2023, of a new provisional key performance indicator that shows the completion rate of the human resources exceptions, within the delegated authority of the entity, that are submitted to the human resources exception log. The Administration considers this recommendation to be implemented pending the release of the additional provisional key performance indicators and requests its closure in April 2023, when the supporting documentation will be made available to the Board.

history.sg_progress: The Administration continues its work to improve the guidance to entities on the delegated authority for human resources exceptions. The regular updates to the guidance provided to entities on their exercise of the delegated authority to make human resources exceptions and the upgrades to the reporting tool (the human resources exception log) now constitute a continuous exercise for the Business Transformation and Accountability Division in collaboration with all policy and business owners, as well as the Office of Information and Communications Technology for the technological solution. In parallel, the Administration has improved the monitoring of reporting of human resources exceptions by enhancing the key performance indicator to monitor timely compliance for reporting, in February 2022, and completeness of reporting, in April 2023, by showing the completion rate for the submission of human resources exceptions within the entities’ authority in the human resources exception log. In addition, the Administration is working on strengthening the escalation component of the delegation of authority monitoring response mechanism and will pilot this on the reporting and follow-up of human resources exceptions.

history.recommendation_text: The Board recommended that the Administration continue to strengthen the guidance and monitoring of entities in reporting exceptions in order to improve entities’ compliance with the reporting requirements.
history.administration_response: The Administration would like to emphasise that in its view the recommendation is implemented – but that updating guidance is a continuous process. Significant progress has been made in the guidance on human resources exceptions hosted on the revamped 18 BTAD Square since the original recommendation was issued in 2020. The regular updates provided to entities on their exercise of the delegated authority regarding human resources exceptions and the upgrades to the reporting tool (the human resources exception Log) are now in the continuous improvement phase. In the fourth quarter of 2023, the Business Transformation and Accountability Division endorsed a new approach for more accessible and transparent communication of updated guidance. It consists of an iterative review and publication of human resources exceptions guidance per category and type of exception. The review is a continuous process, with additional guidance and expansion to new categories of the exceptions issued at regular intervals several times a year following a consultation and clearance process with human resources experts in the Office of Human Resources and the Human Resources Service Division in the Department of Operational Support. After developing the new format for this iterative and continuous review of human resources exception guidance at the end of 2023, the first publication in the new format on the revamped 18 BTAD Square SharePoint site took place in April 2024.
history.board_assessment: Given that the new audit recommendation overlaps and is an enhanced version of this recommendation, the Board considers this recommendation to be overtaken by events.
